then.text: Your sloop took second on Anguilla Day. The first place was an inch longer. We're appealing to the weather.
Rival Kincaid has lost his bet and his sail, and my sloop is the fastest in Road Bay. You've made this island proud.
Take the pennant. It flies on the winner's mast, and sometimes at the bar.

else.text: Last thing: Kincaid's been boasting in the bay. Go and teach him. He's out by the boats, north of town.

then.text: A sloopling! A young racer, with a sail and an attitude. Every sloop starts as one of these.

else.text: A boat needs a heart. Catch a sloopling along the shore, a young racer, and show me. It'll know the wind.
Sail's done. Now the plank. The carpenter by the harbour has a spare, she'll lend it to a friend.
First thing: a sail. The sailmaker's near the boats. Mind the pins.
Welcome to Sandy Ground. Boat racing is our national sport. The sloops are built from memory, no plans, and raced with a crew sitting out on planks.
Anguilla Day is coming. I need a sail, a plank, a young sloopling for luck, and someone to beat the cocky rival. Take the job, and the sloop's yours to sail.

then.text: Sail's in the boat. Mind the stitching.

else.text: A sail for the race? Here. Dacron, three-cornered, and a patch where the last skipper got stuck on a nail.
A racing sloop's mainsail is enormous, and the mast is held up with prayer and a rope. I sew sails, not miracles.

then.text: That plank's been sat on by a hundred crews. It's got character.
A plank for the crew to sit on, out over the water? Take this one. Teak. A little worn. A lot lucky.

else.text: Plank? Come back when you've got the sail. I'm not giving a plank to someone without a boat.
The racing sloop's crew sit on planks stuck out of the side to keep it upright. If you fall off, you swim. If the skipper falls off, he swims faster.

angu_fisher.text: Spiny lobster, caught in pots. We're careful: no berried females, a closed season, and a size limit. Lobster's too good to waste.
The lobster here is grilled on the beach with butter and garlic, and served with peas and rice. Don't ask for a fork.

angu_goat.text: A goat regards you with the calm of an animal that has outlived three governments and one invasion.

angu_kid.text: Anguilla Day is on the thirtieth of May and there's a big race in the bay. I watch from the shore with a fish sandwich. Good seats.
My grandad says the sloops used to be built on the beach without a drawing. He says a lot of things.

angu_home.text: Back to Brize Norton? The RAF flight leaves from the airport on the dot of whenever.
Head home to RAF Brize Norton?

then.text: Right-o. The goats will wave from the runway.

else.text: Take your time. We'll be here.
